metadata.description: Full academy knowledge pack for child safety, vulnerable persons, abuse, neglect, grooming, exploitation, and disability harm.

pack.title: Children and Vulnerable Persons Reviewer Knowledge Pack
pack.purpose: Provide reviewer knowledge for child safety, vulnerable persons, abuse, neglect, exploitation, grooming, trafficking, and disability harm.
required_evidence: A literal chunk-level span showing direct abuse, neglect, exploitation, grooming, trafficking, forced labor, discrimination, or endangerment.
A scene or dialogue span that makes the child or vulnerable person the clear target of the harmful action.
A cross-sentence pattern that links a later sentence to the earlier vulnerable target or harmful act.
insufficient_evidence: A neutral mention of a child, teenager, parent, or guardian without harmful treatment.
A medical, educational, documentary, court, or police reference that only records the topic.
A fictional, dreamlike, or flashback scene that does not endorse the harmful act.
reviewer_heuristics: Anchor the finding to the exact literal phrase that shows harm, coercion, neglect, or exploitation.
Do not treat parental discipline as abuse unless the text clearly shows harm, humiliation, fear, or endangerment.
Look for grooming, isolation, secrecy, gifts, control, or recruitment when exploitation is implied.
Treat disability mockery and discrimination as separate from general rudeness when a protected person is targeted.
Use the scene, dialogue, and cross-sentence context to determine whether the conduct is harmful, protective, or neutral.
positive_examples: Direct abuse: يضرب الطفل بقسوة — explicit physical abuse.
Grooming: أعطي الطفل هدايا لكي يبقى سرًا معي — manipulative grooming.
Neglect: تركته بلا طعام أو ماء طوال اليوم — direct neglect.
Disability mockery: يضحكون على الإعاقة أمامه — deliberate disability humiliation.
Forced labor: أجبر القاصر على العمل ليلًا — forced labor of a minor.
Trafficking: نقلوه بين المدن لاستغلاله — trafficking-style exploitation.
negative_examples: Educational lecture: يشرح المعلم كيف نحمي الطفل من الأذى — protective education.
Medical examination: يفحص الطبيب الطفل بعد الإصابة — clinical context only.
Court testimony: يعيد الشاهد العبارة داخل المحكمة — quoted legal evidence.
Historical narration: يصف الوثائقي واقعة قديمة عن الإهمال — historical account only.
Fictional rescue: تنقذه القصة في النهاية — protective fiction with no endorsement.
Parenting guidance: يشرح الأب قواعد البيت بهدوء — discipline without explicit harm.
common_false_positives: A parent setting rules or discipline without humiliation, fear, or injury.
A doctor, teacher, or reporter discussing child safety in a factual way.
A quotation, flashback, or fictional villain line that the story rejects.
A mention of disability without mockery or discriminatory framing.
A neutral scene where the child or vulnerable person is protected rather than harmed.

glossary_relationships.note: Signals a minor rather than an adult.
Relevant when abuse or mockery targets disability.
Strong when a vulnerable person is used for gain.
Relevant when secrecy, gifts, or control appear.
Strong when movement or control for exploitation appears.

article_mapping.note: Use when child or vulnerable-person content also affects rating sensitivity.
Primary mapping for abuse, neglect, grooming, trafficking, forced labor, and endangerment.
Use when the content humiliates, bullies, isolates, or discriminates against a vulnerable person.

reporting_guidance: Report the shortest literal span that demonstrates the harmful act or harmful intent.
Explain whether the target is a child, vulnerable adult, disabled person, parent, or guardian.
If the context is educational, medical, documentary, court, news, or clearly protective, say so and suppress or downgrade the finding.
Use article 6 for direct abuse or exploitation and article 17 for dignity and discrimination issues.
